children: Hornbeck Offshore Services executed a series of financing and capital-structure actions tied to the closing of its mergers. The company increased its first-lien revolving credit facility to $125 million and lifted uncommitted incremental capacity to $175 million, enhancing liquidity. It also amended its first- and second-lien facilities to permit the merger and adopted updated Jones Act warrant frameworks, including anti-dilution protections tied to dividends. Concurrently, Hornbeck terminated the legacy Helix $120 million ABL facility with no amounts outstanding, simplifying the post-merger capital structure.
